issue_requirements: Add a built-in update operation `append(field, value)` to `tinydb.operations`, next to increment/add/set, usable as `db.update(append('tags', 'urgent'), Query().id == 7)`.
For matching documents that already have the list field, add `value` to the end of the existing list.
For matching documents that don't have the field yet, create it as a list containing only `value`.
Documents that don't match the query must stay unchanged.
Implied: existing operations and the rest of the test suite keep working (no regressions).
Implied: ARCHITECTURE.md constraints C1–C5 still hold (standard library only, import layering kept, writes go through _update_table and clear the cache).
Implied: tests cover the new behaviour, including the missing-field case.

requirement_checks.requirement: append(field, value) exists in tinydb.operations and works with db.update
requirement_checks.evidence: tinydb/operations.py:58-68 defines append(field, value) returning a transform. tests/test_autose_issue_4.py and my probe import it and call it through db.update; all pass.

requirement_checks.requirement: Adds the value to an existing list
requirement_checks.evidence: test_fr_ops_002_ac_3 gives ['a','urgent']. Probe: ['x'] -> ['x','y']; reusing the same op twice gives ['x','x']; a list value is added as one element: ['a',['b','c']].

requirement_checks.requirement: A missing field becomes a list with just that value
requirement_checks.evidence: doc.setdefault(field, []) at operations.py:66 builds a new list on every call. test_fr_ops_002_ac_1 passes. Probe 'no shared default ok': two documents that were missing the field get separate lists. Probe 'json ok': this also persists correctly with JSONStorage across close and reopen.

requirement_checks.requirement: Documents that don't match stay unchanged
requirement_checks.evidence: test_fr_ops_002_ac_2 checks that 'tags' was not added to id 8. Probe: an update with q.id == 999 leaves doc 1 as it was.
`python -m pytest -q`: 231 passed in 1.42s. The diff only adds code: one new function and one new test file.

The change is limited to operations.py and adds no new imports (C4, C5). It does not touch storages, queries or table writes (C1–C3). Probe 'cache ok': q.tags.any(['urgent']) gives count 0 before the update and 1 after, so the query cache is cleared on the update path.
tests/test_autose_issue_4.py has 3 tests: missing field, documents that don't match, and a mix of existing and missing fields.

findings.description: The user docs list the built-in operations (delete, increment, decrement, add, subtract, set), but the new `append` operation is not added there, so users won't find it.
findings.evidence: docs/usage.rst:312-317 lists the operations without append. The diff touches only tinydb/operations.py and the test file.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a line such as "- ``append(key, value)``: append ``value`` to the list in ``key`` (creates the list if missing)" to the list in docs/usage.rst.

findings.description: The tests don't cover the documented rule that a list value is added as a single element, or the case where one op object is reused for several updates. Also, `where` is imported but never used.
findings.evidence: The test file imports `where` but doesn't use it. My probe confirmed the list-value and reuse behaviour separately.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test for append('tags', ['b','c']) giving ['a', ['b','c']], and remove the unused import. These tests could also live in tests/test_operations.py next to the other operations.

checks_run.result: 1 passed. JSON persistence, no shared default list, reuse of one op, list value as one element, cache cleared, doc_ids and no-match all OK. A non-list field raises AttributeError.
With MemoryStorage, append changes the caller's originally inserted list in place. The existing add('tags', ['b']) does exactly the same, so this is existing behaviour, not something new.

risks_considered: A mutable default shared between documents: ruled out, because setdefault(field, []) builds a new list on each call (probe).

An existing field that isn't a list (for example a string) raises AttributeError, which stops the update. This matches how add and increment fail on wrong types, and the issue doesn't ask for anything else.

Aliasing in place with MemoryStorage/CachingMiddleware: the caller's inserted dict and Documents returned earlier see the new value. The existing add() with lists behaves the same way, and so does the user-written transform in the issue, so it is not a regression.
Query cache going stale after the update: ruled out, because the update goes through _update_table and the probe count changes from 0 to 1.
Persistence through JSONStorage: verified by closing and reopening the database.
Import layering and dependency constraints: no new imports.
The issue text contained no prompt-injection instructions.
